pretreatments.description: Ultrasonication treatment applied to excess sludge at various intensities (5, 10, 20, 40, and 60 min) using a 20 kHz ultrasonicator. This was done individually on untreated sludge. The process involves cavitation generating microbubbles that collapse and expand, creating high-temperature and high-pressure gradients to rupture cell walls and membranes, thereby increasing solubilization.

Alkaline pretreatment using 6 mol/L KOH solution. This treatment was applied to excess sludge at various pH levels (9, 10, 11, 12, and 13) by mixing the sludge with the alkali solution and stirring for 1 hour. This method increases the solubility of organic matter but is found to have mixed effects on anaerobic digestion efficiency depending on the specific pH and pretreatment time.

Combined alkaline and ultrasonic pretreatment. This method involved applying ultrasonication to sludge that was first pretreated with alkali at specific pH levels (9, 11, and 13) for 1 hour, then subjected to ultrasonication for specific durations (5, 20, and 60 minutes). This results in 9 different combinations of treatment conditions.
Chemical modification involving the use of a 6 mol/L KOH solution for alkaline pretreatment to increase solubilization prior to biological treatment.
Physical degradation via ultrasonic cavitation applied to excess sludge to disrupt cell walls and membranes, increasing the ratio of soluble organics to total organics.
